Content:
Now, let [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] be two complementary angles. If
[MATH: 5m\angle A - 2m\angle B =310^\circ,]
what is [MATH: m \angle B?]

Content:
There are two variables in the equation above. But we can eliminate one of them using the relationship between complementary angles.

Content:
Since [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] are complementary angles, we have

Content:
[MATH: m∠A + m∠B|= 90^{∘}; m∠A|= 90^{∘} − m∠B.]

Content:
Substituting [MATH: m \angle A =90^\circ - m\angle B] into [MATH: 5m\angle A - 2m\angle B =310^\circ,] we obtain:

Content:
[MATH: 5m∠A − 2m∠B|= 310^{∘}; 5(90^{∘} − m∠B) − 2m∠B|= 310^{∘}; 450^{∘} − 5m∠B − 2m∠B|= 310^{∘}; 450^{∘} − 7m∠B|= 310^{∘}; 7m∠B|= 140^{∘}; m∠B|= 20^{∘}]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: m\angle B = 20^\circ.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] are complementary angles, we have [MATH: m \angle A + m \angle B = 90^\circ.]

Substituting [MATH: m \angle B = 2m \angle A,] we obtain:

[MATH: m∠A + m∠B|= 90^{∘}; m∠A + 2m∠A|= 90^{∘}; 3m∠A|= 90^{∘}; m∠A|= 30^{∘}]

Therefore, [MATH: m∠B|= 2m∠A; = 2(30^{∘}); = 60^{∘}.]

[MATH: m∠B|= 2m∠A; = 2(30^{∘}); = 60^{∘}.]

Since [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] are complementary angles, we have

[MATH: m \angle A + m \angle B = 90^\circ.]

[MATH: m∠A + m∠B|= 90^{∘}; m∠A + 2m∠A|= 90^{∘}; 3m∠A|= 90^{∘}; m∠A|= 30^{∘}]

Therefore,
[MATH: m∠B|= 2m∠A; = 2(30^{∘}); = 60^{∘}.]
